mainTopic: Witnesses for the new moon and how the new month was announced
overview: The amud opens by asking how many people must vouch for an unknown witness of the new moon. רב פפא says the משנה's 'another' means another pair, and the word 'אותו' in the same משנה backs him up. A story about רבי נהוראי seems to show one person vouching alone. The גמרא explains that a second witness was really involved, and learns from the story that שבת may be broken for this even when it is uncertain the trip will help. עולא and רב כהנא then teach that even one ordinary person is believed when he reports that בית דין sanctified the month, because people do not lie about things that will come out. A ברייתא tells how the ביתוסים bribed false witnesses, which led the חכמים to accept only known witnesses. A new משנה describes the torch signals that relayed the news from mountain to mountain until the כותים ruined the system and messengers replaced it. The גמרא proves that מַשִּׂיאִין means burning. It then asks why torches were lit only after a 29-day month, and רבי זירא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can one person vouch for a witness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's 'send another with him': one person alone should not be believed, and a ברייתא speaks of 'his witnesses' in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is one witness believed? A ברייתא teaches about a case where a man came to testify, and his witnesses came with him to vouch for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה said that if the court does not know a new-moon witness, someone else is sent with him to vouch for him. The גמרא asks how one single person could be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vouching for a witness is itself testimony, and testimony normally needs two people. The ברייתא supports this by saying 'his witnesses' in the plural, which seems to clash with the משנה's word 'another' in the singular.

keyTerms.meaning: a story or incident used as a source

steps.confusionAlert: The new-moon witness is not the one being questioned here. The question is about the person sent to vouch that this witness is trustworthy.

phrases.english: But is one witness believed?!
phrases.notes: This is about the 'another' person in the משנה who is sent along to vouch for the unknown witness.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
There was an incident in which he came to testify
and his witnesses were with him to testify about him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's wording 'send another with him' (from before this section).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Testimony needs two witnesses, and a ברייתא says 'his witnesses' in the plural, so one person should not be enough.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'another' means another pair
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה's 'another' refers to another pair of witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What does 'another' mean? Another pair.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by reading 'another' as 'another pair.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself does not change. Two people are still needed to vouch for a witness. Only the reading of the משנה's word changes, so it now matches the ברייתא's 'his witnesses.'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
What is meant by 'another'? Another pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה

steps.title: Support from the word 'אותו' in the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב פפא: the משנה's 'if they don't recognize אותו' must mean that pair of witnesses, so 'another' likewise means another pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you don't say so, what does 'if they don't recognize him' mean? If 'him' means one witness, is one witness believed? The word 'judgment' is written about it. Rather, 'him' must mean that pair. So too, 'another' means another pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב פפא's reading fits the משנה itself. Another singular-sounding word in the same line, 'אותו,' also has to mean a pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting the new month is called 'משפט,' and judgment requires two witnesses. So the new-moon witness himself must be two people, which means 'אותו' refers to a pair. If 'אותו' is a pair even though it sounds singular, then 'אחר' can be a pair too.

keyTerms.meaning: so too it stands to reason (supporting logic)
him / that one (word in the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'אותו' and 'אחר' in the משנה refer to pairs, because new-moon testimony is 'משפט' and needs two witnesses.

phrases.english: So too it stands to reason,
for if you do not say so,
then 'if they do not recognize him,'
what does 'him' mean?
If you say 'him' means one witness,
is one witness believed?
'Judgment' is written about it.
Rather, what does 'him' mean? That pair,
so too: what does 'another' mean? Another pair.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב פפא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's reading that 'אחר' means a pair
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'אותו' in the same משנה, which must mean a pair because new-moon testimony is 'משפט'

steps.title: The story of Rabbi Nehorai in Usha
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the two-witness rule from a ברייתא where רבי נהוראי went by himself to vouch for a witness on שבת in אושא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is one person not believed? A ברייתא teaches about רבי נהוראי, who went with the witness to vouch for him on שבת in אושא!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges from the other direction. A story seems to show that one person was enough to vouch for a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names only רבי נהוראי going with the witness, as if he vouched alone. That would contradict the conclusion that a pair is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: אושא, a town where the סנהדרין sat

phrases.english: And is one witness not believed?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
There was an incident with רבי נהוראי
who went with the witness
to testify about him on שבת in Usha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 2-3 that two people are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a pair is needed to vouch for a witness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נהוראי seems to have vouched alone, which suggests one person is enough.

steps.title: A second witness came but was not named
steps.stepSummary: Another witness came with רבי נהוראי but was left out of the story out of respect for רבי נהוראי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: there was another witness with רבי נהוראי. He was not mentioned because of רבי נהוראי's honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer that רבי נהוראי did not really vouch alone. A second witness was with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story only seems to show one witness. The second witness was left out so as not to place an ordinary person next to רבי נהוראי as his equal. The two-witness rule stays in place.

phrases.english: They say:
As for רבי נהוראי, another witness
was with him,
and the reason the ברייתא does not mention him
is because of the honor of רבי נהוראי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי סָהֲדָא אַחֲרִינָא הֲוָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the facts of the story
steps.terutzMaskana: A second, unnamed witness traveled with him.

steps.title: רב אשי: the second witness was already in Usha
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers differently: the second witness was already waiting in אושא, and רבי נהוראי traveled there to join him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: there was another witness already in Usha, and רבי נהוראי went to join together with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to the רבי נהוראי story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אשי's answer, nobody was left out of the story. The second witness was already in אושא, and רבי נהוראי's trip completed the pair. Either way, the rule stands that two people are needed to vouch for a witness.

keyTerms.meaning: to join together (to complete a pair)

steps.whatToRemember: Two people are always needed to vouch for a new-moon witness. Both answers explain the רבי נהוראי story without giving up this rule.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
As for רבי נהוראי, another witness
was already in Usha,
and רבי נהוראי went
to join together with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי סָהֲדָא אַחֲרִינָא הֲוָה בְּאוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzMaskana: He joined a witness who was already in אושא, completing the pair.

steps.title: Then why tell the story at all?
steps.stepSummary: If a second witness was already waiting in אושא, the story of רבי נהוראי seems to teach nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of telling us this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבי נהוראי story adds if רב אשי's explanation is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אשי, two witnesses were present after all, so the normal rule was simply followed. If nothing unusual happened, there seems to be no reason to record the story.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? / What does this teach?

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if רב אשי is right that the second witness was already in אושא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer by saying it makes the story pointless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two witnesses were there as usual, the story teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The story teaches that we break שבת even when it is uncertain
steps.stepSummary: The story teaches that רבי נהוראי could break שבת even though it was not certain the other witness would be there.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that we do not break שבת when the outcome is uncertain. The story teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story does teach something new: you may break שבת for עדות החודש even when it is not sure the trip will help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second witness might not have shown up, and then רבי נהוראי's walk would have done nothing. We might have thought that a doubtful case does not allow breaking שבת. The story shows that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבי נהוראי story teaches that for עדות החודש you may break שבת even when it is not certain the trip will help.

phrases.english: You might have said:
we do not break Shabbat in a doubtful case,
phrases.notes: The doubt is whether the other witness would really be in אושא.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 by naming what the story teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new teaching in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We do not break שבת when it is uncertain the action will help.
steps.terutzMaskana: For עדות החודש, we break שבת even in a doubtful case.

steps.title: עולא reports that the month was sanctified in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: עולא arrives in בבל and reports, by himself, that the month was sanctified in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came, he said: They sanctified the month in the West.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. עולא, one person alone, reports which day ארץ ישראל made ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the theme of how many witnesses are needed. Here a single person reports, not about seeing the moon, but about what בית דין decided. In the next step, רב כהנא explains why one person is enough for that.

phrases.english: When Ulla came, he said:
They sanctified the month in the West.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: one person reporting בית דין's decision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא alone reports that ארץ ישראל sanctified the month.

steps.title: רב כהנא: Even an ordinary person is believed about this
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that anyone, not just a great person like עולא, is believed alone about when בית דין sanctified the month, because people do not lie about things that will come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Obviously עולא, a great man, is believed. But even an ordinary person is believed. Why? People do not lie about something that is going to be found out anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains that one witness is enough here, and that the person does not need to be someone special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two witnesses are needed, as with seeing the moon. But whether בית דין sanctified the month is a public fact that will soon be known everywhere. A lie would be exposed quickly, so people do not lie about it, and one ordinary person is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say; obviously
A matter that is likely to come out

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that people do not lie about something that will come out (עבידא לאגלויי) is a well-known rule used in many places in ש"ס.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
It is not necessary to say that Ulla,
who is a great man, is believed.
Rather, even an ordinary person
is also believed.
What is the reason?
Any matter that is going to come out,
people do not lie about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why עולא's report alone was accepted, and widens it to anyone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any single person is believed that בית דין sanctified the month, because people do not lie about things that will come out.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that one person who comes from far away and reports that בית דין sanctified the month is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: If one person comes from the end of the world and says בית דין sanctified the month, he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks of "one" person with no special status, so it matches רב כהנא's rule that any single person is believed. Coming from far away does not reduce his credibility.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)

steps.whatToRemember: One ordinary person is believed when he reports that בית דין sanctified the month. A ברייתא supports this.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
If one person came from the end of the world

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר קִדְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ —
phrases.english: and said: The court sanctified the month,
he is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא's rule with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's rule that an ordinary single person is believed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: one person from far away is believed

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Testimony used to be accepted from anyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying that originally they accepted moon testimony from anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: At first, they accepted testimony about the new month from any person, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה to explain its next line. This sets up the ברייתא about the ביתוסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes on to say this changed because the ביתוסים caused trouble. The גמרא now wants to know exactly what trouble they caused.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony about seeing the new moon

phrases.english: At first they would accept testimony about the month
from any person, and so on.
phrases.notes: "And so on" points to the rest of the משנה: this stopped once the ביתוסים started causing trouble.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ מִכׇּל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, moon testimony was accepted from anyone.

steps.title: The ביתוסים hire two false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how the ביתוסים paid two men 400 זוז to testify falsely, one of them from the חכמים' side and one from their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What trouble did the ביתוסים cause? Once they tried to mislead the חכמים. They hired two people for 400 זוז, one of ours and one of theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains what the ביתוסים did. It begins the story of how they tried to trick the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ביתוסים wanted בית דין to set ראש חודש on the wrong day, so they bought false testimony. They hired one witness from their own group and one from the חכמים' side, which shows how far they were willing to go.

keyTerms.meaning: ביתוסים, a group that disagreed with the חכמים

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What corruption did the Boethusians cause?
Once the Boethusians tried
to mislead the Sages.
They hired two people
for four hundred zuz,
one of ours, and one of theirs.
phrases.notes: "Ours" means a person from the חכמים' side; "theirs" means one of the ביתוסים.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה קִלְקוּל קִלְקְלוּ הַבַּיְיתּוֹסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the trouble mentioned in the משנה from Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ביתוסים hired two false witnesses to mislead the חכמים about the new moon.

steps.title: Our witness gives an absurd description and reveals the bribe
steps.stepSummary: Their witness testifies and leaves. Our witness describes the moon as a strange animal and then shows the 200 זוז he was paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their witness gave his testimony and left. They told our witness: Tell us how you saw the moon. He said: I was going up at מעלה אדומים and saw it lying between two rocks. Its head was like a calf, its ears like a kid, its horns like a deer, and its tail was between its legs. I looked at it, got scared, and fell backward. And if you don't believe me, here are 200 זוז tied up in my cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. Our witness, when questioned, gives a ridiculous description and then reveals the money he was paid, exposing the plot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין asked each witness to describe what he saw. Their witness testified and left. Our witness described the moon like an animal, a description that makes no sense, and then showed the bribe money. This revealed that the whole testimony was bought.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name: the ascent of Adumim

phrases.english: Theirs gave his testimony and left.
To ours, they said:
Say how you saw the moon!
He said to them:
I was going up at Ma'ale Adumim,

phrases.aramaic: וּרְאִיתִיו שֶׁהוּא רָבוּץ בֵּין שְׁנֵי סְלָעִים,
phrases.english: and I saw it crouching between two rocks.
Its head was like a calf,
phrases.notes: He is describing the moon as if it were an animal, which makes no sense.

phrases.english: its ears were like a kid,
its horns were like a deer,
and its tail lay between its thighs.
I peeked at it, got frightened, and fell backward.
And if you do not believe me,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי מָאתַיִם זוּז צְרוּרִין לִי בִּסְדִינִי.
phrases.english: here are two hundred zuz tied up in my cloak.
phrases.notes: This is his half of the 400 זוז the ביתוסים paid, and it shows the testimony was bought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's story from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our witness exposed the ביתוסים' plot with an absurd description and the bribe money.

steps.title: The Sages ask the witness why he did this
steps.stepSummary: After the honest witness reveals the bribe, the חכמים ask him what pushed him to get involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Who pushed you into this?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask the honest witness why he agreed to take the bribe and go along with the plan. This question sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He just showed them the 200 זוז, which proves the ביתוסים hired him. The חכמים want to know why a loyal person would join their plot at all.

keyTerms.meaning: pushed you or obligated you (to do this)

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים of בית דין.

phrases.english: Who pushed you into this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the witness revealing the 200 זוז bribe.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the witness took the ביתוסים' money and joined their plan.

steps.title: The witness explains he went to warn the Sages
steps.stepSummary: He heard the ביתוסים wanted to fool the חכמים. He joined the plot so he could expose it and keep dishonest people from misleading them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I heard that the ביתוסים were trying to mislead the חכמים. I said: I will go and let them know, so that unworthy people do not come and fool the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The witness answers that he joined the plan on purpose so he could expose it from the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was never really on the ביתוסים' side. He took the job so they would not hire someone dishonest in his place, and then he told the truth in court.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I heard that the ביתוסים were seeking
to mislead the Sages,
I said: I will go and let them know,
phrases.notes: He means: I will take the job myself and then tell the חכמים the truth.

phrases.english: lest people come
who are not decent
and mislead the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁבִּקְּשׁוּ בַּיְיתּוֹסִים לְהַטְעוֹת אֶת חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He joined the plot to expose it and to keep dishonest people from taking the job.

steps.title: The witness keeps the money and the hirer is punished
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים let the honest witness keep the 200 זוז as a gift. The man who hired him is to be whipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The 200 זוז are given to you as a gift, and the one who hired you will be stretched out on the post.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים rule on how the story ends. The honest witness is rewarded and the plotter is punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness did not do what he was paid for, but the חכמים still let him keep the money as a gift. The ביתוסי who hired him is stretched on the post for lashes because he tried to corrupt בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: and the one who hired you
will be stretched out on the post (for lashes)

phrases.english: They said to him: The two hundred זוז
are given to you as a gift,
and the one who hired you
will be stretched out on the post.
phrases.notes: This is how a person was tied down to receive lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָאתַיִם זוּז נְתוּנִין לְךָ בְּמַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים react to the witness's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The honest witness is rewarded with the money and the plotter is punished.

steps.title: Enactment to accept only known witnesses
steps.stepSummary: Because of this incident, the חכמים enacted that moon testimony would be accepted only from witnesses known to בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time they enacted that they would accept testimony only from people who are known.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a new rule. From then on, moon testimony comes only from witnesses whom בית דין recognizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the circle opened in step 12. At first, testimony was accepted from anyone. The ביתוסים' plot showed that this was dangerous, so the rule was narrowed to known witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: they made a תקנה (a rabbinic enactment)
those who are known (to בית דין)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule that moon testimony comes only from known witnesses was made because of the ביתוסים' attempt to bribe witnesses.

phrases.english: At that time they enacted
that they would not accept
except from those who are known.
phrases.notes: He means witnesses whom בית דין recognizes as reliable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מְקַבְּלִין אֶלָּא מִן הַמַּכִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the story with the תקנה it caused.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Moon testimony is accepted only from witnesses known to בית דין.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the background of the משנה's change from accepting anyone to accepting only known witnesses.

steps.title: New משנה: torches at first, messengers later
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that at first the new month was announced with torches. After the כותים ruined that, messengers were sent instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Originally they would light torches. Once the כותים ruined it, they enacted that messengers would go out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It explains how people far away used to learn that בית דין had sanctified the month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first method was fast torch signals from mountain to mountain. The כותים ruined it, so it was replaced with messengers, which is slower but more reliable.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Originally
they would light torches.
Once the כותים ruined it,
they enacted that messengers would go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a new topic: announcing the new month.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torch signals were replaced by messengers after the כותים sabotaged them.

steps.title: How were the torches lit?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how the torch signals actually worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: How would they light the torches?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks its own question to set up a detailed description of the torch system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. The משנה simply wants to explain the method it just mentioned.

phrases.english: How would they light the torches?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about the torches mentioned in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method of the torch signals.

steps.title: The torch method, mountain to mountain
steps.stepSummary: They tied together cedar poles, reeds, pinewood and flax, lit them on a mountaintop, and waved the torch until the next mountain answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: They bring long cedar poles, reeds, pinewood and beaten flax, and tie them with a string. He goes up to the mountaintop, lights them, and waves the torch back and forth and up and down. He keeps going until he sees his friend doing the same on the second mountain, and so on with the third mountain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question by describing exactly how the torch signal was made and passed along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The materials were chosen to burn brightly. The waving made the signal easy to recognize. Each torchbearer kept going until he saw the next mountain pick up the signal, so the message moved along a chain of mountains.
steps.whatToRemember: The torches were passed from mountain to mountain. Each person kept waving until he saw the next mountain answer.

phrases.english: They bring long poles of cedar,
and reeds, and pinewood,
and beaten flax.
And he ties them with a string
and goes up to the top of the mountain
and lights the fire with them.
And he waves it back and forth and up and down,
until he sees his friend

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן בְּרֹאשׁ הָהָר הַשֵּׁנִי,
phrases.english: doing the same on the top of the second mountain,
and so too on the top of the third mountain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the משנה's question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bright torches were lit and waved on mountaintops and relayed from one mountain to the next.

steps.title: From which mountains were the torches lit?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks where the torch signals were lit, so we know the route of the message.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where would they light the torches?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a new practical question: where exactly were the torches lit? This sets up the next step, which gives the route.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained how a torch was made and waved. Now the משנה wants the path of the signal, mountain by mountain.

phrases.english: And from where would they light the torches?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the description of how the torch was waved with a question about where it was done.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The list of places where the torch signals were lit.

steps.title: The mountain-to-mountain route of the signal
steps.stepSummary: The signal went from הר המשחה to סרטבא, גרופינא, חוורן and בית בלתין. From there the man waved the torch until the whole גולה was lit up.
steps.simpleTranslation: From הר המשחה to סרטבא, from סרטבא to גרופינא, from גרופינא to חוורן, and from חוורן to בית בלתין. From בית בלתין they did not move on. Instead the man there waved the torch back and forth and up and down, until he saw the whole גולה in front of him like one big bonfire.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the chain of mountains that passed the signal along. At the last station, בית בלתין, the man kept waving until he saw the whole גולה lit up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were set stations as far as בית בלתין. After that there was no fixed next mountain. The man kept signaling until he saw that communities everywhere had picked up the message and lit their own fires.

keyTerms.meaning: the Mount of Olives, by ירושלים
they did not move on from there
the Diaspora, Jews living outside ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: The torch system was a relay. Each mountain passed the signal to the next, until the whole גולה knew that ראש חודש had been declared.

phrases.english: From the Mount of Olives to Sartava,
and from Sartava to Gerofina,
and from Gerofina to Ḥavran,
and from Ḥavran to Beit Baltin,
and from Beit Baltin they did not move on from there,
rather, he would wave it back and forth and up and down

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁהָיָה רוֹאֶה כׇּל הַגּוֹלָה לְפָנָיו
phrases.english: until he would see the whole Diaspora before him
like a bonfire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fixed route ran from הר המשחה through סרטבא, גרופינא and חוורן to בית בלתין. From there the man waved the torch until the whole גולה was lit.

steps.title: How do we know מַשִּׂיאִין means lighting a fire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for a source that the משנה's word מַשִּׂיאִין means burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we see that 'מַשִּׂיאִין' is a word for burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about the משנה's wording. How do we know that מַשִּׂיאִין means lighting a fire? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Literally, the root נשא usually means 'to carry' or 'to lift'. So the גמרא wants proof that here it means 'to burn'.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
From where is it understood that 'masi'in'
is a word meaning burning?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּ״מַשִּׂיאִין״ לִישָּׁנָא דִּיקוֹד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא, starting with the משנה's word מַשִּׂיאִין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that מַשִּׂיאִין means burning.

steps.title: Proof from דוד burning the idols
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'ויִּשָּׂאֵם דוד ואנשיו', and the תרגום renders it 'and דוד burned them'. So the root means burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'וַיִּשָּׂאֵם דוד and his men', and we translate it: 'And דוד burned them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that uses the same root, וַיִּשָּׂאֵם. The Aramaic תרגום translates it as 'burned them'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the תרגום. It reads וַיִּשָּׂאֵם as burning, not carrying. So the same root in the משנה, מַשִּׂיאִין, means lighting fires.

keyTerms.meaning: and he took them up (here: burned them)
and we translate (in the Aramaic תרגום)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Vayisa'em David and his men,'
and we translate: 'And David burned them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרגום of וַיִּשָּׂאֵם is 'burned them', so the root means burning.

steps.title: Torches only for a month declared on time
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that torches were lit only for a month declared on its proper day. They were lit on the night after ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Torches were lit only for a month that was seen at its proper time, to sanctify it. And when were they lit? On the night of its added day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two rules. Torches were lit only when ראש חודש was declared on the 30th day. They were lit on the night that would have been the 31st day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On time' means the moon was seen on the 30th day. That makes the old month 29 days, a חסר month. The torches went up the following night, the night that would have been the extra day, the עיבור, if the month had been full.

keyTerms.meaning: at its proper time, on the 30th day
to sanctify it as ראש חודש
on the night of its added day, the night that would begin the 31st

steps.confusionAlert: 'לְאוֹר' here means 'the night of', not 'daylight'. The torches were lit at night.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Torches are not lit

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל הַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁנִּרְאָה בִּזְמַנּוֹ לְקַדְּשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: except for a month that was seen at its time, to sanctify it.
phrases.notes: 'At its time' means the 30th day, so the month before had only 29 days.

phrases.english: And when do they light them?
On the night of its added day.
phrases.notes: This is the night after the 30th, the night that would have started day 31 in a full month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: when the torch system was actually used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torches were lit only when ראש חודש was declared on the 30th day, after a 29-day month. They were lit on the following night.

steps.title: Why no torches after a full month?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as saying torches mark only a 29-day month, not a 30-day month, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that we do it for a deficient month but not for a full month? What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא: torches were lit after a חסר month but never after a מלא month. It then asks for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It would seem that news of any ראש חודש should be spread. So the גמרא wants to know why a full month is left out of the torch system.

phrases.english: Is this to say that for a deficient month we do it,
but for a full month we do not do it?
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּאַחָסֵר עָבְדִינַן אַמָּלֵא לָא עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא of step 26 and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why torches were not lit after a full, 30-day month.

steps.title: רבי זירא: a גזירה because of ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the rule is a גזירה. It is tied to a ראש חודש after a 29-day month that falls on ערב שבת, when the torches must wait until מוצאי שבת. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It is a גזירה because of a ראש חודש after a חסר month that falls on ערב שבת. When do they light then? At מוצאי שבת. Because if you say we light for a full month too, people would come…
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins to answer. He says the rule is a rabbinic גזירה, and he describes the case behind it. The sentence breaks off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ראש חודש (day 30) falls on Friday, the torches should go up Friday night. Lighting fire on שבת is forbidden, so they wait until מוצאי שבת. רבי זירא is starting to show that lighting torches for full months too would lead to a mix-up in this case. The details of the mix-up come next.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
at the end of שבת, מוצאי שבת

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It is a decree because of a New Moon after a deficient month
that falls on Shabbat eve.
When do they do it? At the end of Shabbat.
For if you say we should do it for a full month as well,
they would come
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the mistake people would make is spelled out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ חָסֵר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exclusion of full months is a גזירה. It is tied to a ראש חודש after a חסר month that falls on ערב שבת, when the torches are delayed until מוצאי שבת. The full reasoning continues on the next amud.
